qs.q: During an outbreak investigation of watery diarrhea in a coastal community, clinicians isolate a curved, oxidase-positive Gram-negative rod from rice-water stools. What is the precise pathophysiological mechanism responsible for the massive fluid loss in this condition?
o: Direct destruction of intestinal epithelium by a potent cytotoxin
Water and electrolyte hypersecretion caused by increased intracellular cAMP
Inhibition of protein synthesis through a Shiga-like ribosome inactivator
Elevated mucosal permeability due to invasive cellular damage
Osmotic fluid retention from malabsorption of unfermented carbohydrates
qs.e: The cholera toxin stimulates adenylate cyclase, raising intracellular cAMP levels and causing active chloride and water secretion into the intestinal lumen.

qs.q: An outbreak investigation reveals that a pathogen is transmitted primarily via the faecal-oral route and survives remarkably well on dry surfaces and in water. Which characteristic best explains this environmental stability?
o: Presence of a viral reverse transcriptase
Acquisition of a host-derived cell membrane
Icosahedral capsid symmetry with spike proteins
qs.e: Non-enveloped (naked) viruses lack a fragile lipid bilayer, making them tough and resistant to drying, detergents, and gut pH. Enveloped viruses are fragile and easily destroyed by heat, drying, and detergents.

qs.q: During an outbreak investigation in a crowded slum, health officers examine individuals infested with body lice. Which severe systemic infection is transmitted transcutaneously by Pediculus humanus corporis?
qs.e: The body louse transmits Rickettsia prowazekii, causing epidemic typhus, as well as relapsing fever and trench fever via transcutaneous routes. Lyme disease is tick-borne rather than louse-borne.
